source: High Country Fly Fishing Experts like Due South Outfitters

conditions.overall: High Country streams in Watauga, Ashe, and Avery Counties are running at typical early-June levels with cold, clear water at elevations of 3,300–4,000 ft. Delayed Harvest regulations on key streams lift June 6, 2026, opening harvest season on heavily stocked waters.

top_flies.name: Elk Hair Caddis
top_flies.note: Reliable dry fly for hatchery-supported and wild trout on High Country streams in early summer

top_flies.name: Pheasant Tail Nymph
top_flies.note: Standard subsurface pattern for stocked and wild trout in pool-riffle-run sequences

top_flies.name: Hare's Ear Nymph
top_flies.note: Versatile nymph; effective on freshly stocked fish and in faster pocket water

top_flies.name: San Juan Worm
top_flies.note: High producer on stocked fish and in hatchery-supported sections after stocking events

top_flies.name: Zebra Midge
top_flies.note: Effective on clear, low water when fish are selective; fish as a dropper below a dry

top_flies.name: Woolly Bugger
top_flies.note: Streamer option for larger browns and stocked fish; swing through pools and deeper runs

top_flies.name: Adams Parachute
top_flies.note: All-purpose dry fly well suited to High Country freestone streams throughout early summer

tactics: June 6 marks the end of Delayed Harvest catch-and-release restrictions on the Watauga River, Helton Creek, Big Horse Creek, and other DH waters — you may now harvest fish; switch tactics accordingly.
High Country streams near Boone (3,300–4,000 ft) run 1–2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC waters — adjust hatch timing and fly selection to account for cooler water temps.
Fish the Valle Crucis section of the Watauga River early in the day to avoid crowds; it sees lower pressure than the Boone access points and offers classic pool-riffle-run sequences.
On stocked hatchery-supported waters, dead-drift nymphs like the Pheasant Tail or Hare's Ear through the head and tail of pools where fish stack after stocking.
Use barbless hooks or pinch barbs before fishing — especially on Delayed Harvest and wild trout waters — to reduce handling stress and protect the fishery.
Keep fish in the water as much as possible; wet your hands before handling, use a rubber-mesh net, and hold the fish facing current until it swims off under its own power.
On clear, low flows, downsize tippet and flies (midges #18-22) and approach pools from downstream to avoid spooking fish in gin-clear water.

waters.name: Watauga River (Valle Crucis Section)
waters.note: 1.2-mile Delayed Harvest section upstream of Boone; harvest opens June 6, 2026. Lower pressure than the Boone section. Classic pool-riffle-run water; good early-morning access.

waters.name: Watauga River (Laurel Creek Confluence Section)
waters.note: 1.0-mile DH section near Boone; harvest opens June 6, 2026. High accessibility but higher angler pressure; fish early or on weekdays.

waters.name: Helton Creek
waters.note: Largest DH fishery in Ashe County at 8 miles; 7,500 fish stocked annually. Harvest opens June 6, 2026. VA line to New River. Brook, rainbow, and brown trout available.

waters.name: Big Horse Creek
waters.note: Has both a Delayed Harvest section (SR 1324 Bridge downstream) and a Hatchery Supported section on the same stream — know the boundary before wading to avoid a regulation violation.

waters.name: North Fork New River
waters.note: 20-mile hatchery-supported corridor in Ashe County; part of 22,911-fish county stocking program. Good exploratory water with less pressure than the DH fisheries.

waters.name: North Toe River (Avery County)
waters.note: Two separately managed stocked sections; 5,170 fish stocked in March and May. Lower section (SR 1164 to Mitchell County Line) is most productive by fish count at 4,396 fish/year. All tackle, 7-fish creel.

waters.name: Linville River
waters.note: Catawba headwaters in Avery County; high-elevation cold water holds trout well into summer. Part of Avery's 10,709-fish 2026 stocking program.

waters.name: Elk River
waters.note: Avery County stream draining toward Tennessee; stocked as part of Avery's three-watershed trout program. Good option for variety and scenery.

waters.name: Davidson River
waters.note: Lower-elevation WNC hatchery-supported water; gravel lot fills before first light on opening day. Not in the High Country — conditions run 1-2 weeks ahead of Watauga/Ashe/Avery streams.

waters.name: Wilson Creek
waters.note: Hatchery-supported WNC stream; lower elevation than High Country waters. Mentioned as a key Opening Day destination for early April stocked-fish action.

elevation_note: High Country streams near Boone (3,300–4,000 ft) run 1–2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC waters — hatches, water temps, and seasonal transitions all lag behind streams in the Pisgah and Nantahala areas.
stocking_note: Avery County's North Toe River, Linville River, and other hatchery-supported waters were stocked in March and May 2026. Watauga County's 14 hatchery streams received 11,606 fish in 2026. Ashe County's 15 waters received 22,911 fish in 2026. Delayed Harvest waters across all three counties were heavily stocked during the Oct 2025–June 2026 C&R season; harvest opens June 6, 2026.
